items.title: A year on, where does Trump's Gaza peace plan stand?
items.description: On Oct 10, 2025, Israel began pulling its troops from parts of Gaza as a peace agreement it signed with Hamas went into effect . A year later, it has expanded its occupation to about 70 per cent of the Palestinian territory — one of its many violations of that ceasefire. The 20-point peace plan envisaged by United States President Donald Trump , titled ‘ Comprehensive Plan to End Gaza Conflict ’, has not just remained stalled; it has been torn apart by Washington’s own ally Israel. At the time, Trump had touted the plan as a breakthrough that would bring “eternal peace” to the Middle East. He later launched his own military campaign alongside Israel in the war against Iran. The initial phase resulted in a ceasefire on Oct 10, 2025 and secured the release of the last remaining captives seized in Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel, along with freedom for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and detainees held by Israel. While the October 10 agreement pertained only to the first phase of the peace plan, the roadmap laid out by Trump had offered the world a glimmer of hope for some semblance of calm in the shattered Palestinian territory. Yet a year on, many of the plan’s goals have yet to materialise, including securing an Israeli withdrawal and rebuilding Gaza. Dawn takes a look at which guarantees have been achieved and what remain unfulfilled promises to the Palestinians, and to peace. What was the plan? The first phase of Trump’s 20-point plan included a suspension of all military operations, Israeli withdrawal from part of ‌the enclave, captive and prisoner releases and a surge in aid. While the first phase of the plan remains incomplete due to the large presence of Israeli troops, the US had announced moving on to the second phase in January, which also remains stalled. The Gaza peace plan 72 hrs to return all hostages 250 life-sentence prisoners freed 1,700 post-Oct 7 detainees freed 15 : 1 Gazan remains per hostage remains Phase 1: immediate steps War ends Military operations suspended, battle lines frozen, Israeli forces pull back to an agreed line. Point 3 Hostages and prisoners All hostages, living and deceased, returned within 72 hours of Israel accepting. Israel then releases prisoners and detainees. Points 4-5 Aid floods in Full aid at no less than Jan 19, 2025 levels. Run by the UN, Red Crescent and neutral bodies. Rafah reopens both ways. Points 7-8 Hamas amnesty Amnesty for members who disarm and commit to coexistence. Safe passage for those who want to leave. Point 6 ↓ Phase 2: transition and security Interim governance Technocratic Palestinian committee runs services, overseen by a "Board of Peace" chaired by Trump, with Tony Blair among members. Point 9 Demilitarisation Hamas has no governing role. Tunnels and weapons sites destroyed. Weapons decommissioned under independent monitors, with a buy-back scheme. Point 13 Stabilisation force International Stabilisation Force trains vetted Palestinian police and helps secure borders with Israel and Egypt. Point 15 Phased IDF withdrawal Israel withdraws in stages tied to milestones, keeping a security perimeter. No occupation or annexation. Point 16 If Hamas rejects the plan Aid and reconstruction proceed anyway in areas handed from the IDF to the ISF. Point 17 ↓ Phase 3: rebuilding and political future Reconstruction Economic development plan by an expert panel, plus a special economic zone with preferential tariffs. Points 10-11 Right to stay No one forced to leave Gaza. Those who leave are free to return. Point 12 Regional guarantee Regional partners guarantee Hamas and other factions comply. Point 14 Political horizon Interfaith dialogue, and a possible pathway to Palestinian statehood once Palestinian Authority reforms are done. Points 18-20 Source: full text of the plan as released by the White House, published in Dawn, Sept 30, 2025. " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> How well has the ceasefire held? Barely. The plan aimed to bring a halt to Israeli military operations after a two-year bombing campaign — widely determined to be a genocide — killed over 74,000 Palestinians. However, near-daily attacks have killed more than 1,460 Palestinians, including 300 children , since the ceasefire took effect on Oct 10. Israel attacked the enclave on 337 of the past 365 days, based on a tally compiled by Al Jazeera and reports by AFP and Palestinian Wafa news agency. This leaves only 28 days without reported attacks over the year-long period up to Oct 9. Israeli attacks on Gaza, Oct 10, 2025 – Oct 9, 2026 · shaded days had reported attacks – days with reported attacks – quiet days (no reported attacks) – of the 365 days had attacks Attacks reported Quiet day Quiet days come from a list compiled from Al Jazeera's reporting. The list has 28 days, all before Oct 5. October 2026 has no quiet days (AFP and WAFA reported strikes from Oct 6-9). Every other day in the window is shaded as an attack day. " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> Israel claims its strikes have targeted Hamas, accusing the group of trying to carry out attacks and rearm. Hamas denies this, and forums such as the United Nations have also condemned Israel’s continued violence. On the other side, five Israeli ​soldiers have been killed by Palestinian fighters or in combat since the ceasefire, according to the Israeli military. Has Israel withdrawn from Gaza? The first ⁠phase of Trump’s plan foresaw Israel withdrawing to a so-called “yellow line”, allowing Israeli forces to retain control of 53 per cent of Gaza. However, as of July, it had expanded its occupation to nearly 70pc of the besieged enclave, according to maps analysed by NPR . This isn’t just covert movement; Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unabashedly directed his military in May to expand its control to 70pc of the strip. Part of this was already done in March — when the world’s attention was caught by the US-Israel war against Iran — and Israel marked a new “ orange line ”, taking effective control of 11pc of Gaza’s territory beyond the yellow line. This collage shows a map of Gaza with the yellow line under the peace plan (L) and a map of the territory depicting Israeli control up till the “orange line”, issued by UN OCHA on Sept 30, 2026 (R). — X/WhiteHouse/ochaopt.org The creeping military presence has ​ uprooted more Palestinians, squeezing the population of 2 million into a shrinking coastal strip where they shelter in tents and damaged buildings. A September report by The New York Times based on satellite images said Israel constructed six new military outposts in its self-designated orange zone after the ceasefire, many on the rubble of homes and villages. Moreover, Israel-backed Palestinian militias and opposed to Hamas use the Israeli-held zone to launch attacks on the area where most of the Palestinian population lives. From the start of the ceasefire through April, at least 196 Palestinians, including 18 women and 43 children, were killed near the Yellow Line, according to figures verified by the United Nations’ rights office . Since October 2025, accessible and undamaged cropland has fallen from 601 hectares to 448 hectares, according to a June assessment by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO). It noted that the loss of 25.5pc reflected reduced access to farmland since the ceasefire, “associated primarily” with the expansion of the yellow line. As recently as last month, members of Israel’s far-right government called for the annexation of parts of the Gaza Strip and for forces to “go to war” in the occupied West Bank. “I would like us to annex at least as far as the yellow line in Gaza and as far as the Litani River in Leba­non, because if a war ends along the same lines where it began, what will deter the enemy from going to war again?” Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said in a podcast for the Israeli news site Ynet . Has the flow of aid resumed? After Israeli policies led to a famine in Gaza City during the war and starved hundreds to death across the strip, the first phase of Trump’s peace plan was supposed to enable the entry of “full aid” into the territory. “Entry of distribution and aid in the Gaza Strip will proceed without interference from the two parties through the United Nations and its agencies, and the Red Crescent, in addition to other international institutions not associated in any manner with either party,” read the plan. However, while the flow has resumed, many foreign aid groups still struggle to work in the territory and say their staff or supplies continue to be rejected. In Gaza, humanitarian assistance is the key lifeline for most families. Remember that “orange line” Israel drew? International organisations, including humanitarian groups, are required to coordinate their movements with the Israeli military to deliver aid in the area between the orange line and the yellow line. According to a report by global hunger watchdog IPC, expansion of humanitarian assistance improved household food consumption since a December 2025 IPC analysis, shifting from IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) to Phase 3 (Crisis) levels. However, all five governorates — Rafah, Khan Younis, Deir al-Balah, Gaza and north Gaza — are still classified in IPC Phase 3, with 212,000 people remaining in Phase 4. This collage shows maps by the IPC for its reports on Gaza strip covering the July-August 2025 period (L) and April-June 2026 period (R). More than 1.4m people (67pc of the population) were expected to face high levels of acute food insecurity (Phase 3 or above) through December 2026, up from 1.2m in the mid-April–June period, IPC said. It noted that despite the flow of aid, food security coverage has largely declined, falling from a peak of 2.13m people reached in November 2025 to 1.49m people in May 2026. Further reductions were also expected due to funding constraints and uncertainty surrounding the renewal of operational authorisations for 37 international non-governmental organisations (INGOs). The IPC report further said that, on average, Gaza received 227 aid trucks per day, as opposed to the requirement of 600 daily trucks outlined in the peace plan. According to a UN monitor , the highest number of trucks arriving in Gaza between October 2025 and August 2026 was 334, recorded on Dec 20. Monthly trends for the number, weight and pallets of aid arriving at the intended destination in Gaza under the UN2720 Mechanism between October 2025 and O — screengrab via tracking.un2720.org With winter approaching, UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov told the UN Security Council (UNSC) last month that “the health situation remains critical” in Gaza. He noted that “restrictions on the entry of critical humanitarian items continue to impede the scale-up of the humanitarian response”, including preparations for the rainy season. Last week, the UN-run World Health Organisation (WHO) also urged Israeli authorities to “release the pressure on medical supplies”. Essential medicines and even prosthetics — needed widely after Israel’s war left about 5,000 amputees — are denied by Israel, which insists that they could be used by Hamas fighters. Disarmament of Hamas Later phases of the peace plan foresaw Hamas disarming and new governance by a Palestinian body overseen by the Trump-led Board of Peace . Israel was to gradually withdraw based on milestones linked to demilitarisation, handing territory to a temporary International Stabilisation Force (ISF). However, those plans have also stalled despite Trump hailing a “historic” agreement in July on the disarmament of Hamas and other groups. Hamas had agreed in July to hand over its weapons to be stored under the control of the Palestinian technocratic government, but the Israeli occupation appears to be a sticking point as both sides dispute the sequencing of the plan’s implementation. Tel Aviv objected to the Board of Peace’s text that called for it to begin a phased withdrawal and demanded “full demilitarisation” of Hamas before it pulled back its troops. The Trump-led board then assured Netanyahu that Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza would only begin after Hamas’s complete disarmament. Subsequently, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner met with Hamas and Israeli leaders in August, but without any breakthrough as both sides stuck to their demands. Israel insisted on not withdrawing until Hamas surrendered all its weapons — a condition reportedly agreed to by Kushner — and on continuing military operations as it saw fit. On the other hand, the Palestinian group wanted Israel to abide by the ceasefire first. Where is the ISF? Under Trump’s plan, the Israeli military was to “progressively hand over the Gaza territory it occupies” to the multinational ISF. “The ISF will work with Israel and Egypt to help secure border areas, along with newly trained Palestinian police forces,” the text stated. While some plans for the ISF have taken shape, the force has yet to be assembled. There is a commander — US Major General Jasper Jeffers — and Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Albania, Kosovo and Uganda have committed personnel. Each contingent requires individual Israeli approval to enter Gaza. Jeffers has said that the long-term plan is for the ISF to comprise 20,000 troops and train 12,000 Palestinian police officers. The plan has reportedly been marred by countries’ concerns over the legitimacy and the mandate of the mission. Just a day after Trump unveiled the text of his peace plan, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar seemingly distanced Pakistani decision-makers from the roadmap and called for the inclusion of amendments proposed by a group of Muslim countries. The remarks came amid reports that the deal before Hamas was significantly different from the one the US and a group of Muslim countries had previously agreed on, due to Netanyahu’s intervention. About two months later, he said Pakistan was ready to commit its troops to ISF, but distanced the country from any role in disarming the Palestinian resistance group. “We are not ready for that. This is not our job, but of the Palestinian law enforcement agencies. Our job is peacekeeping, not peace enforcement.” — Dar The deputy premier also maintained that the decision on deploying forces could only be taken once ISF’s mandate was decided. The US held a conference in December 2025 to discuss the force’s key aspects, but it failed to produce a mandate that would satisfy both Israel and potential troop contributors. The July plan, called the Gaza Roadmap , said the ISF is to be deployed to “separate the Israeli forces” from areas controlled by the technocratic Palestinian governing body, as well as “monitor compliance by all parties with the ceasefire”. Meanwhile, the technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza ( NCAG ) has also yet to enter the enclave. Appointed in January, the US-backed NCAG is led by Ali Shaath , who formerly served as a deputy minister in the Ramallah-based Palestinian ​Authority. Living among ruins “Gaza will be redeveloped for the benefit of the people of Gaza, who have suffered more than enough,” was what Trump’s peace plan promised. A year on, Palestinians are still scavenging in the rubble of wrecked buildings for materials to prop up tents and other ​shelters. A UN assessment in April estimated the recovery and reconstruction needs at $71.4 billion over the next 10 years, with $26.3bn to restore essential services and critical infrastructure. In sharp contrast to the estimate, the Board of Peace in September unveiled a $2.45bn Gaza recovery plan meant to span over six months, covering only a fraction of the cost outlined by the UN. This screengrab from a Board of Peace presentation given in February 2026 shows a phased reconstruction plan for Gaza. — boardofpeace.org As per the UN report, Gaza’s economy contracted by 84pc while 50pc of the hospitals in the strip remained non-functional; and nearly all schools were destroyed or damaged, along with more than 371,888 housing units. UN further estimated that the impact of the two-year-long assault had set Gaza back by 77 years and displaced about 60pc of its population. Thousands of Palestinians live in an estimated 2,000 damaged , bombed-out buildings that are at risk of collapse. Just last month, at least 20 people , including five children, died after an apartment building in Gaza City collapsed from damage sustained in earlier Israeli strikes. Satellite images of Gaza port on Oct 8, 2023 and during the war (Aug 25, 2025), and of Rafah before (Aug 20, 2023) and during the war (Sept 30, 2025). — GIF made using Claude, with images courtesy Planet Labs PBC via Reuters Future of Gaza For now, the future appears grim. Israel’s right-wing politicians have been ramping up momentum against mass removal of Palestinians through “voluntary emigration”. Last month, Israeli ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Israel Katz called for the expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza, which would be a clear violation of the US-led plan to resolve the conflict. “We are fully prepared to move them out if it becomes possible — by sea, by air, by every way possible. Egypt is not willing, so it won’t be through them,“ Katz said. The calls also came ahead of the Oct 27 general elections in Israel — the first since the 2023 Hamas attacks, over which Netanyahu faces criticism within his country. This screengrab from a Board of Peace presentation given in February 2026 shows a long-term roadmap for redeveloping Gaza. — boardofpeace.org On the global level, Pakistan, along with Egypt, Turkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, has repeatedly called on Israel to fulfil outstanding commitments under the peace plan — which was also endorsed by the UNSC. A joint statement issued last month stressed that Israel should ensure the immediate, safe and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance and early recovery supplies, as well as facilitate the rehabilitation of critical infrastructure. Just days earlier, the Board of Peace had shared comments by Biden-era envoy Brett McGurk, who stressed the roadmap laid out by Trump and backed by the UNSC: Hamas has to relinquish its authority over Gaza; Israeli forces must ultimately withdraw from the territory; the ISF is to provide interim security; and a credible pathway towards Palestinian self-determination must be established. With the Muslim bloc’s attention now largely on other Middle East conflicts , and Trump’s “ peacemaker ” mode overtaken by his threatening posture towards Iran, it remains to be seen when the Palestinians of Gaza will get the promised peace, let alone freedom from occupation. Additional input from Reuters Header image: Made with pictures of an Israeli tank on Israeli side of the Gaza border on Aug 20, 2025, Board of Peace meeting on Feb 19, 2026 and a map of Gaza. — via Reuters

items.title: UTAG-UG threatens strike on October 19 over unpaid allowance
items.description: The University of Ghana branch of the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG-UG) has threatened to withdraw teaching and related services from Monday, October 19, 2026, if the government fails to pay its members’ 2026 Book and Research Allowance. In a notice of intention to embark on industrial action dated October 9, 2026, the association said the planned action was in response to persistent delays in the payment of the allowance. The notice, addressed to the National Labour Commission, said the delay was contrary to a Memorandum of Agreement signed between UTAG and the government in 2020, which provides for the allowance to be paid by the end of August each year. UTAG-UG has given the government until Friday, October 16, 2026, to settle the outstanding payments. “Given the current circumstances, if by Friday 16th October 2026 these monies are not paid, members of UTAG-UG will withdraw all teaching and related services beginning Monday 19th of October 2026,” the notice stated. The letter was signed by the association’s president, Dr. Jerry Joe Harrison, and its secretary, Godfred Bright Hagan. Copies of the notice were sent to the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, the ministers responsible for Employment and Labour Relations, Finance and Education, the Director of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission, and the national president of UTAG. The latest threat follows earlier warnings by the University of Ghana branch over delays in the payment of the allowance, which supports lecturers’ academic and research activities. The proposed withdrawal of services could disrupt teaching and other related academic activities at the University of Ghana if the outstanding payments are not made before the deadline.

items.title: Xi Jinping et le problème du Ciel
items.description: Découvrez Le Grand Continent . Des idées et des analyses que l’on ne trouve nulle part. Mais que vous verrez bientôt partout. Dans votre boîte mail à partir de 8 euros par mois Depuis le début du XXIe siècle, un mot vieux de trois millénaires, oublié du lexique républicain puis communiste, fait son retour dans les débats intellectuels de la République populaire de Chine et affleure jusque dans la phraséologie officielle : tianxia , « ce qui est sous le Ciel ». Il désignait autrefois l'espace terrestre soumis à la loi du Ciel à travers son unique mandataire, le souverain régnant depuis le centre du monde. Réinvesti avec un opportunisme qui s'accommode d'incohérences, le Tout-sous-le-Ciel de l'antique royauté des Zhou sert aujourd'hui à dire ce que la Chine pense d'elle-même, de l'Occident et de l'ordre mondial qu'elle appelle de ses vœux. Derrière ce nouvel universalisme se tient une conviction presque aussi ancienne : l'unité serait la seule condition de l'ordre, de la paix et de la puissance. Du Tout-sous-le-Ciel à la nation, et vice-versa De la royauté de l'âge du bronze à la chute de l’empire en 1911, tianxia a désigné une étendue aux contours flous, sur laquelle s'exerçait l'autorité rituelle et morale du souverain. Le tianxia est ce qu'une dynastie « obtient » ou « perd » au gré du mandat céleste ( tianming ), doctrine forgée par les chefs des Zhou pour légitimer leur victoire sur le peuple Shang vers 1045 avant notre ère : le Ciel confie le mandat à un homme vertueux et le retire à ses descendants s'ils viennent à démériter. Les contrées situées hors de l'espace où rayonne la vertu du souverain lui renouvellent leur allégeance par le tribut. Le mot recouvre ainsi à la fois une cosmologie morale et un idéal de sujétion universelle. À la fin de la dynastie des Qing, au début du siècle dernier, cette construction idéologique se heurte aux canonnières et aux traités inégaux. Liang Qichao (1873-1929) et les réformateurs de sa génération reprochent à leurs aînés d'avoir vécu dans un imaginaire périmé : à force de se croire le centre du monde civilisé, les Chinois ont ignoré la loi darwinienne de la concurrence entre États-nations. Il faut donc inventer d'urgence ce qui manque au pays : un nom, des frontières, une langue nationale, une ethnie majoritaire, une histoire continue et un ancêtre fondateur, l'Empereur Jaune. L'historien américain Joseph Levenson a résumé l'histoire intellectuelle de la Chine moderne par ce passage du tianxia au guojia , l'État-nation. Depuis une vingtaine d'années, le mouvement s'inverse. Devenue un État-nation prospère et puissant, la Chine réhabilite le passé impérial contre lequel elle s'était construite. Encore faut-il nuancer ce rejet : la République populaire avait rejeté le régime, qualifié de « féodal », tout en conservant scrupuleusement les territoires des Qing. L'héritière des frontières impériales en retrouve à présent la rhétorique. Trois voix se font entendre : le discours officiel, qui n’emploie guère tianxia que dans des citations classiques et lui préfère la « communauté de destin pour l'humanité » ; les philosophes et les juristes, qui font du tianxia un système ; enfin, leurs contradicteurs, qui appartiennent eux aussi au milieu universitaire. Ces théoriciens valent mieux que de simples propagandistes, et leurs critiques de l'Occident portent souvent juste, sans qu’ils démontrent pour autant la viabilité de leur propre projet. Le chiffre du bon gouvernement Il suffit d'un seul trait horizontal pour écrire le plus impérieux des chiffres : l'Un, la réalité première, la totalité en germe. Pendant les Royaumes combattants (Ve-IIIe siècle av. J.-C.), il devient le seul point de ralliement d'un monde engagé dans une guerre totale. Le roi Xiang de Liang demande à Mencius comment le monde trouvera son assise ; « Par l'unité », répond le philosophe sectateur de Confucius. Et qui pourra l'unifier ? « Celui qui ne prend pas plaisir à tuer. » La seconde réponse fut sans doute moins écoutée que la première. Les écoles rivales ne débattent plus de la fin, seulement des moyens : les armes ou la vertu. L'échec de l'ordre multipolaire des Printemps et Automnes, avec ses alliances, ses serments, ses otages et ses hégémons, les a convaincus qu'il n'y aurait de paix que par l'absorption de tous les royaumes sous le règne d'un seul. Les Printemps et Automnes du sieur Lü , compilés à la veille de l'unification impériale formulent la déclinaison du principe : une armée a besoin d'un (unique) général et un pays d'un (seul) prince — le monde du Fils du Ciel —, car l'unité produit l'ordre et la dualité ne génère que le chaos. Certes, nul ne se méfiera a priori d'un éloge de l'unité, de l'harmonie ou de la grande Concorde. La difficulté commence quand l'idéal se loge dans des institutions marquées par deux mille ans d'idéologie impériale, puis par un régime répressif. Les lettrés ont débattu de la meilleure manière de gouverner l’empire, et Huang Zongxi (1610-1695) a pu dénoncer l’empereur qui traite le monde comme son bien propre ; mais ces controverses restaient internes à la monarchie. Entre l'Un et le chaos, le tiers était exclu. C'est précisément cet espace médian que la modernité politique occidentale s'est efforcée d'inventer avec le pluralisme et l'équilibre des pouvoirs. Le plan de vol vers une « nouvelle ère » Le texte qui donne au récit contemporain sa forme canonique est le rapport présenté par Xi Jinping au 19e Congrès du Parti, en octobre 2017. On y lit une téléologie en trois temps : plongée dans les malheurs depuis la guerre de l'Opium, la nation chinoise s'est relevée, puis enrichie, pour devenir enfin puissante. Le rapport attribue ces étapes au Parti seul ; ses commentateurs y liront les noms de Mao, de Deng et de Xi. La Chine se rapproche désormais du centre de la scène mondiale et offre aux pays qui veulent se développer sans perdre leur indépendance une « option entièrement nouvelle », une « sagesse chinoise » et une « solution chinoise ». Au milieu du siècle, elle sera une puissance socialiste moderne, « prospère, puissante, démocratique, civilisée, harmonieuse et belle » : le troisième adjectif n'est pas le moins audacieux. L'inflexion autoritaire se cristallise dans une formule empruntée à Mao : « Parti, gouvernement, armée, peuple, études ; est, ouest, sud, nord, centre : le Parti dirige tout. » En chinois courant, les cinq orients veulent simplement dire « partout ». Mais l'oreille rompue à l’esprit lettré y pressent encore un cosmogramme, l'un de ces schémas anciens où le monde s'ordonne autour d'un centre. Là où siégeait le Fils du Ciel a pris place le Parti. Le rapport du Congrès décline ensuite l'unité à toutes les échelles. Les ethnies sont appelées à se serrer « comme les graines d'une grenade » et les religions à se « siniser ». Face à Taïwan, nul ne sera autorisé, en aucun temps et sous aucune forme, à détacher la moindre parcelle du territoire. Au dehors, la Chine promet de ne jamais rechercher l'hégémonie et de bâtir une « communauté de destin pour l'humanité ». Dans sa péroraison, le rapport cite le Livre des Rites : « Quand la grande Voie prévaut, ce qui est sous le Ciel appartient à tous ». Le rapport se conclut par le rappel des 9,6 millions de kilomètres carrés du territoire national : le monde qui est à tous a tout de même les frontières indiscutables de la République populaire. Un monde sans dehors Le plus doué des artisans de cette greffe de l'ordre céleste sur l'État moderne est le philosophe Zhao Tingyang, né en 1961, dont Le Système du Tout-sous-le-Ciel (paru pour la première fois en 2005) a donné au débat sa forme philosophique. Zhao n'appartient pas à l'appareil, mais ses thèses épousent si bien les ambitions du régime que celui-ci n'a guère eu besoin de les commanditer. Son diagnostic est celui d'un monde resté proche de l'état de nature hobbesien, où des États coexistent dans l'anarchie. Il y oppose un ordre « sans dehors » ( wuwai ), au sein duquel aucune nation ne pourrait plus faire peser sur les autres le coût de ses actes, où chacun chercherait à réduire l'hostilité avant d'accroître son gain, et où nul ne progresserait sans que tous progressent avec lui. L'Occident, à ses yeux, n'a connu qu'une politique de l'ennemi, du partage chrétien entre fidèles et païens au « choc des civilisations », et un impérialisme devenu, avec l'hégémonie américaine, « mondialisé ». Le problème tient à la relecture de l'histoire que Zhao s'autorise. La foi dans la « grande unification » ( da yitong ) ne suffit pas, selon lui, à expliquer la longévité de l'unité chinoise ; il lui faut une dynamique objective, qu'il trouve dans un « modèle du tourbillon ». Les peuples des marges auraient été attirés vers la plaine Centrale comme vers l'enjeu d'une compétition, et Mongols ou Mandchous, en conquérant la Chine, n'auraient fait qu'entrer dans le jeu. Le récit change l'expansion en attraction et laisse les armées hors du tableau. Zhao interdit en outre d'appliquer à l'histoire chinoise le concept d'impérialisme, qu'il réserve à l'Occident. Si l'Occident a des empires, la Chine n’a que des vortex. Zhao se défend toutefois de faire le jeu de l'uniformité. Il invoque la distinction, que l’antique texte du Commentaire de Zuo prête au grand ministre Yanzi, entre l'harmonie ( he ), qui accorde des éléments différents, et la conformité ( tong ), qui réduit tout au même. Même si le la chronique de cour qu’il invoque disait en fait autre chose, il tire de cette polarité l’impératif de la protection de la diversité des cultures. Reste le mandat céleste. Zhao cite le Livre des Documents selon lequel le Ciel voit par les yeux du peuple. Encore faut-il savoir comment le peuple s'exprime. Zhao répond par une « démocratie intelligente » tirée du même classique : sur cinq voix, le roi, les ministres et le peuple en ont chacun une, et les deux dernières, réservées jadis à la divination, reviendraient aujourd'hui à la science. Si ces deux voix savantes s'opposent à une décision, on y renonce, même si le roi, les ministres et le peuple l'approuvent à l'unanimité. Variations sur l'Un D'autres auteurs travaillent, avec plus de zèle encore, à réconcilier ce que l'histoire chinoise a opposé. Dès 2005, Gan Yang appelait à « réunir les trois lignées légitimes » ( tong san tong ) : celles de Confucius, de Mao et de Deng. Il emprunte cette formule à Dong Zhongshu, qui l'appliquait sous les Han aux trois premières dynasties. Le philosophe Chen Lai ajoute à ces synthèses une métaphysique de l'Un : dans son Ontologie du ren (2014), la vertu confucéenne d'humanité fait de tous les êtres un seul corps. Le juriste Jiang Shigong, professeur à l'université de Pékin, fournit l’interprétation la plus proche de la version officielle dans un article de 2018 qui commente, parfois de façon poussive et scolaire, le rapport du 19e Congrès. Le chef, le Parti et les masses y forment un seul agent, « organique et unifié », et le communisme n'est plus une société à faire advenir ici-bas mais une foi et une valeur spirituelle. Jiang donne à l'ambition mondiale du Parti deux racines — la tradition confucéenne du tianxia et la croyance communiste en la libération de l'humanité —, et lui assigne pour mission d'étendre la civilisation chinoise à des parties toujours plus nombreuses du monde. Les deux universalismes que l'on croyait rivaux, celui des lettrés et celui des révolutionnaires, fusionnent à l’ère de Xi Jinping. Les objections de l'intérieur Cet enthousiasme pour le tianxia est loin de faire l'unanimité en Chine. En 2015, le prestigieux historien Ge Zhaoguang, de l'université Fudan, publie dans la revue Taïwanaise Sixiang une démolition en règle de « l'imagination du tianxia ». Le tianxia ancien, rappelle-t-il, a toujours reposé sur trois partages : entre le dedans et le dehors, entre les Chinois et les barbares, entre ceux qui commandent et ceux qui obéissent. Les Han et les Tang l'ont élargi à coups d'expéditions, et c'est après avoir écrasé les Turcs orientaux, en 630, que l’empereur Taizong des Tang se vit décerner par les chefs des steppes le titre de « Khan céleste ». Quant au passage du Livre des Rites que cite le rapport du 19e Congrès, il appartient aux rêveries des lettrés, et l'idée d'un monde où « proches et lointains, grands et petits ne font qu'un » est une idée, rappelle Ge, qui n’a jamais pris corps dans l’orthodoxie impériale. Ge voit dans ces théories le fruit de l'essor chinois et d'un curieux transfert : les critiques occidentales de l'impérialisme, de Said à Hardt et Negri, ont nourri en Chine un nationalisme qui annonce, après le siècle américain, celui du tianxia . Il se demande si le tianxia ne deviendra pas un nationalisme drapé dans l'internationalisme, et pose la question que ses promoteurs éludent : qui sera le chef de cette grande famille, qui en fixera les règles, qui fera la justice ? Faute de réponse, le tianxia redeviendra un empire, sous quelque nom qu'on lui donne. La même année, l'historien libéral Xu Jilin tente de sauver le concept de ses défenseurs. Son « tianxia 2.0 » garde l'universalisme de l'ancien et en retranche le centre et la hiérarchie : il repose sur l'égalité souveraine des États et sur la reconnaissance mutuelle, puisque, dans un âge séculier, nul peuple ne peut plus se dire investi du mandat céleste. Un universel qui récuse l'eurocentrisme doit renoncer aussi au sinocentrisme. On peut lui adresser le reproche que E. H. Carr faisait aux utopistes de l'entre-deux-guerres : supposer acquise une harmonie des intérêts que la politique de puissance dément chaque jour. Sur le plan intérieur, sa proposition a pourtant un tranchant réel. Constatant que la grandeur retrouvée n'attire pas les minorités vers le centre, il propose d'étendre le principe « un pays, deux systèmes » aux régions autonomes des frontières. Mais il emprunte ouvertement son modèle aux empires, qui toléraient les coutumes des marges pourvu qu'elles reconnaissent l'autorité du centre. Son tianxia est décentré au-dehors et centré au-dedans. L'Occident au miroir chinois Les critiques chinoises de l'Occident contiennent une bonne part de vérité. Les États-Unis n'offrent aucun leadership crédible sur le climat, ils n’ont adopté aucune politique à la mesure des inégalités dont leur population pâtit, la prédominance du capital sur le politique nourrit un populisme qui menace la démocratie, et l'ordre libéral issu de 1945 n'a jamais paru aussi fragile. La Chine peut se prévaloir d'une tradition qui affirme la primauté du politique sur le capital, et d'investissements massifs dans les technologies vertes, même si elle reste de très loin le premier émetteur mondial de gaz à effet de serre. L'Europe, qui a longtemps cru que la croissance en Chine ferait naître une classe moyenne, et la classe moyenne la démocratie, s'est méprise sur un agenda qui n'a pourtant jamais manqué de cohérence ni de clarté. Mais les démocraties occidentales malades ne prouvent pas la bonne santé d’un pays gouverné par un parti unique. Un capitalisme d'État autoritaire réussi offrirait aux régimes autoritaires, plutôt qu'une sagesse plurimillénaire, un modèle doté d'outils de surveillance et de répression sans précédent. Le prêche et la pratique La coexistence harmonieuse que Pékin n'a pas su accorder à ses propres marges, au Tibet et au Xinjiang soumis à l'assimilation forcée, à Hong Kong remis en 2020 sous son autorité directe, les théoriciens du tianxia la proposent à tous les pays du globe. Dans le monde qui est à tous, quelqu'un doit dire ce qui est commun. Zhao confie le dernier mot à des savants dont il ne dit pas qui les nomme ni sur quelles bases ; Jiang Shigong est plus franc avec sa pétition de principe : le chef, le Parti et les masses ne font qu'un. La célébration de la grande Unité est aujourd'hui monumentale : unité du passé et du présent, du confucianisme et du marxisme, de l'État et du Parti, du Parti et du peuple, des classes et des ethnies. Le régime qui la prêche manque pourtant d'unité sur un point : entre l'irénisme des intentions affichées au monde et la rigueur d'un pouvoir qui ne souffre aucune divergence, la dualité reste flagrante. L’article Xi Jinping et le problème du Ciel est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Supreme Court releases report documenting judicial, institutional reforms
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court of Pakistan (SC) has released its report, “Journey Through Reform and Innovation 2026”, documenting the judicial and institutional reforms undertaken from November 2024 to September 2026. The report provides a comprehensive account of the SC’s reform efforts, highlighting progress in case management, reducing the backlog of pending cases, digital transformation, institutional accountability and public access to justice. It documents the implementation of an 86-point Reform Action Plan, supported by a structured governance mechanism, dedicated working groups and regular reviews of reform initiatives. The report also records measurable progress in judicial performance, including a substantial increase in case disposals, greater focus on long-pending cases, expanded digital services and stronger data-driven performance monitoring. It also highlights key national initiatives advanced through the National Judicial (Policy Making) Committee, including time-bound disposal of prioritised cases, establishment of Model Trial Courts, responsible use of artificial intelligence and the development of judicial analytics. Significant progress has also been made in modernising judicial procedures, improving access to court services and strengthening institutional collaboration. The report further documents initiatives aimed at facilitating litigants, enhancing transparency, expanding international judicial cooperation and promoting a more responsive justice system. The document serves as an institutional record of the reform process, capturing both measurable achievements and the continuing work required to strengthen the efficiency, accessibility, predictability and responsiveness of justice delivery in Pakistan.

items.title: Police arrest inspector, two civil guards over extortion in Imo
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Imo State Police Command has arrested a police traffic warden, Inspector Chinwe Ejiogu, and two personnel of the State Civil Guard Corps over alleged extortion and harassment of a motorist in Owerri. The arrests followed the circulation of a viral video showing the officers allegedly harassing and attempting to extort a motorist who was said to be driving without a driver’s licence. In a statement signed by the state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Henry Okoye, the command condemned the conduct captured in the video, describing it as unacceptable and contrary to the standards of discipline and integrity expected of law enforcement personnel. Okoye identified the police inspector as Ejiogu, attached to the Shell Camp Divisional Police Headquarters, while the two civil guard personnel were identified as Kelechi Nzediagwu and Onyedikachi Chibuike. He said the three suspects were being detained at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) as investigations continued. “The Imo State Police Command is aware of a viral video in which a police traffic warden and two personnel of the State Civil Guard Corps were captured harassing and extorting a motorist allegedly driving without a driver’s licence in Owerri on October 8, 2026,” the statement said. According to Okoye, the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Audu Garba Bosso, has directed the command’s Complaint Response Unit (CRU) to investigate the incident. The command also urged the affected motorist to report to the unit and provide relevant information to assist the investigation. It said appropriate disciplinary action would be taken upon the conclusion of the investigation. The police reiterated that no traffic violation justified extortion, harassment or abuse of office, warning personnel to discharge their duties in accordance with the law and treat members of the public with respect. The command further urged members of the public to report incidents of police misconduct through the appropriate channels, assuring them that allegations of misconduct would be treated seriously. The post Police arrest inspector, two civil guards over extortion in Imo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Just In: Lagos varsity lecturers suspend strike
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Lecturers under the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, in three Lagos State-owned universities have suspended their industrial action and are set to return to classrooms with immediate effect. The development has brought relief to students and parents affected by the disruption of academic activities. The affected institutions are Lagos State University, LASU, Lagos State University of Education, LASUED, and Lagos State University of Science and Technology, LASUSTECH. The unions announced the suspension on Friday, while expressing appreciation to the media, civil society organisations, CSOs, traditional rulers, students, parents and other stakeholders for their support throughout the negotiations. It said the collective efforts of these groups contributed significantly to the negotiation process, which centred on improved staff welfare and the implementation of outstanding academic agreements. In a statement jointly issued by Olusegun Babalola, Coordinator, Steering Committee, ASUU-LASU; Grace Abimbola, Acting Chairman, ASUU-LASUED; and Murisiku Onigemo, Chairman, ASUU-LASUTECH, the unions said: “Following the official suspension of our industrial action today, the leadership and entire membership of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, in Lagos State-owned universities wish to express our profound gratitude to the general public, institutional leaders, and key stakeholders who stood firmly by us throughout the negotiation process. “Our struggle for improved staff welfare and the implementation of vital academic agreements has reached a significant milestone, largely due to the collective support of well-meaning individuals and organisations. We wish to express our deepest appreciation to the following: “The Press and Broadcasting Organisations: We thank you for your objective, timely, and investigative coverage. Your platforms ensured that our grievances were accurately communicated to the public and policymakers, helping to keep the discussions balanced and constructive. “Civil Society Organisations (CSOs): We are grateful for the solidarity, advocacy, and unwavering commitment to social justice demonstrated by the Joint Action Front (JAF), Education Rights Concern (ERC), Campaign for Democratic Workers Rights (CDWR), and other pro-worker organisations. Your defense of quality public tertiary education provided valuable support for our cause. “Our Revered Traditional Rulers: We honour our royal fathers for their timely interventions, fatherly counsel, and behind-the-scenes diplomatic efforts. Your wisdom helped bridge communication gaps during critical moments of the impasse. “Students, Parents, and Other Stakeholders: We deeply appreciate your resilience, patience, and understanding throughout this period. We recognise the sacrifices you have made and reaffirm that our struggle remains focused on securing improved staff welfare and a better future for public university education in Lagos State. “As our members return to the classrooms with immediate effect, we reaffirm our commitment to academic excellence and quality university education. We also look forward to continued engagement with the Lagos State Government to ensure the full resolution of all outstanding issues relating to our welfare package. “Once again, we appreciate everyone who stood with us throughout this struggle. Your solidarity and support have been invaluable.” The post Just In: Lagos varsity lecturers suspend strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Passengers groan as flight delays, cancellations worsen
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Domestic air travellers are lamenting frequent flight delays and cancellations across airports in the country, with many expressing frustration over prolonged waiting times and disrupted travel plans. Saturday Vanguard also observed that departure halls at several airports across the country have been crowded in recent times, with many stranded and delayed passengers wearing long faces. A visit to the domestic terminals of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Monday, lent credence to the development, as passengers waited for updates on delayed flights. At the domestic terminal of the Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport, Abuja, Tuesday, the departure hall was crowded, with travellers expressing concern over the frequency of flight disruptions. For instance, one of the passengers, Eze, said his flight had been delayed both on his journey from Lagos to Abuja and on his return trip. He said: “My flight was delayed while I was going to Abuja from Lagos. It was delayed as I am returning. I am stressed, honestly. And I am not alone. Delay announcements are many, about four in two hours today. Terrible.” Another passenger, Jeremiah, whose flight from Warri to Lagos was disrupted, Sunday, said he was forced to spend additional money after the flight was rescheduled to the following day. He said: “I had to part away with another money after my flight scheduled for 5pm on Sunday was shifted to the next day. I needed to be in Lagos by 9am on Monday because I had an important meeting to attend.” Recently, a passenger, Segalink, also took to X, formerly Twitter, to express frustration over a prolonged delay on an Air Peace flight from Asaba to Lagos. He wrote: “Air Peace is interesting. Flight P47863 from Asaba to Lagos which was scheduled to depart at 15:00 on 26/09/2026 (yesterday) kept being rescheduled allegedly due to maintenance and the majority of the passengers slept at the airport in the hope of flying only to be told around 12am that they would fly by 5am this morning. “Unfortunately, that promise wasn’t fulfilled until almost 9am today. These were passengers who bought tickets for a 10am flight originally from Asaba to Lagos. No refreshments or hotel accommodation were provided. Is this how we will continue? These are folks who will not permit you to board if you are 15 minutes late to the counter.” Recall that the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA’s, Summary of Domestic Airline Flight Disruptions Operations for August, which showed that domestic airlines collectively recorded 4,801 disruptions out of 7,961 operated flights. Air Peace recorded the highest number of disruptions, with 1,337 delayed or cancelled flights out of 1,864 operated during the month. United Nigeria Airlines delayed or cancelled 951 of its 1,231 operated flights, while Enugu State-owned Enugu Air recorded 586 disruptions out of 878 operated flights. ValueJet disrupted 438 of its 767 operated flights. Akwa Ibom State-owned Ibom Air recorded 257 disruptions out of 560 operated flights, while Arik operated 301 flights, of which 188 were delayed and one was cancelled. However, the airlines faulted the statistics, saying most of the disruptions were caused by factors beyond their control. The post Passengers groan as flight delays, cancellations worsen appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: En Hongrie, la presse libre refait surface après plus d’une décennie de musellement
items.description: Au long de ses trois mandats, le très droitier Viktor Orbán a méthodiquement bâillonné la presse indépendante. Depuis son départ du pouvoir en avril, elle en sort renforcée. Les médias proches de l’ancien Premier ministre, eux, périclitent.

items.title: Démarrage du 3e concours de scénarios «Ecrire pour l’écran»
items.description: Diletta D’Ascia et Nidhal Chatta annoncent le démarrage, le 15 octobre 2026, de la troisième édition du concours international de scénarios de courts métrages «Écrire pour l’écran», qu’ils organisent en collaboration avec Cinémasters – Académie de l’acteur et du cinéma. Les auteurs de toutes nationalités sont invités à explorer le thème de «L’héritage — patrimoine et mémoire en Méditerranée». Et la date limite de dépôt des candidatures est fixé au 10 avril 2027 à minuit. Gratuit et ouvert à toutes et à tous, sans limite d’âge, le concours s’adresse aussi bien aux auteurs émergents qu’aux scénaristes plus expérimentés. Il entend promouvoir l’écriture cinématographique, encourager de nouvelles voix et favoriser le dialogue entre les cultures à travers des récits destinés au grand écran. L’héritage ne se limite pas aux monuments et aux traces visibles du passé. Il comprend également les traditions, les langues, les savoir-faire, les récits familiaux, les souvenirs et les identités qui se transmettent d’une génération à l’autre. Il interroge ce que nous recevons, ce que nous choisissons de préserver et ce que nous transmettons à notre tour. Au cœur de cette réflexion, la Méditerranée apparaît comme un espace de rencontres, d’échanges, de migrations et de métissages, où les histoires individuelles et collectives se croisent depuis des siècles. Fiction ou documentaire, approche intime, historique, sociale ou contemporaine : les auteurs sont libres d’aborder le thème selon leur propre sensibilité et leur regard sur le monde. Les candidats peuvent soumettre un scénario original et inédit de court métrage, de fiction ou documentaire, rédigé dans la langue de leur choix. Les projets doivent compter entre 3 et 20 pages, hors page de titre, et être envoyés au format PDF. Le dossier comprend le scénario, une note d’intention d’une page maximum et une fiche auteur. Chaque participant peut présenter un seul projet et la participation est gratuite. Les œuvres doivent être écrites par les participants eux-mêmes. L’utilisation d’outils d’intelligence artificielle pour générer tout ou partie du texte est interdite La précédente édition, consacrée au thème «L’Océan dans tous ses états» , a réuni des auteurs de Tunisie, d’Europe, de Madagascar, du Bénin, de Côte d’Ivoire et d’Haïti, confirmant la vocation internationale du concours. Cette expérience a permis de développer des collaborations avec différents acteurs institutionnels et culturels, en Tunisie et en Italie. Pour cette troisième édition, les organisateurs souhaitent poursuivre cette dynamique d’échanges et de transmission, en faisant du scénario un espace de rencontre entre les générations, les cultures et les imaginaires. Informations pratiques L’annonce des résultats et la remise des prix sont fixées au début mai 2027. Le règlement complet peut être demandé à l’adresse suivante : concoursecrirepourlecran@gmail.com L’article Démarrage du 3e concours de scénarios «Ecrire pour l’écran» est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: We’ll make it difficult for Amaechi to campaign in Rivers if… – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has warned that it will be difficult for former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, running mate to the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to campaign in Rivers State if he continues to attack President Bola Tinubu and his supporters. Wike spoke on Friday in Abuja after a meeting with the chairmen of the six area councils of the FCT. He was reacting to comments credited to Amaechi, who allegedly said only thieves and mad people would vote for Tinubu. “If he continues this line, it will be difficult for him to campaign in Rivers. We will not take that. If security agencies and INEC can fold their hands, that’s their business, but we will not allow it,” Wike said. Wike said the remarks were aired on television, and that they went further to include Edo people. “All of us watched on television yesterday where he said it’s only thieves that can vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, only mad people can vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and that if Edo people vote for him, it means Edo people are mad. This is supposedly a vice presidential candidate of a political party seeking to take over power,” he said. The minister said agencies such as the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC should sanction politicians who engage in personality attacks instead of issue-based campaigns. “You see one problem we have in this country is that agencies or commissions should be able to take their functions seriously. Many Nigerians have called INEC to sanction political parties, candidates, or some politicians who, in their campaigns, incite the public or raise matters that are not issue-based,” he said. Wike then challenged Amaechi to account for projects executed while he was governor of Rivers State. “I have challenged him to tell Nigerians where is our $39 million cassava flour mill which you claimed you built? Where is the $10 million you paid to a Cuban company to fumigate Rivers State so there will be no mosquito bite? Where is the N68 billion monorail? Where is the $308 million you sold our gas turbine? “Amaechi has looted the treasury. Ask him why he was indicted by a Judicial Panel of Inquiry and why he went to court to challenge that indictment and lost at the Supreme Court,” Wike alleged. items.title: Trump appoints ‘devoted fan’ Katie Zacharia as press secretary
items.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter. “She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. “She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!” he added, referring to his Make America Great Again movement. Zacharia, a lawyer and communications adviser to Trump’s media company, will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public faces of his second administration. Trump hailed his new spokeswoman’s credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps. Zacharia, in a post on X, thanked Trump for the “distinguished privilege of serving as White House Press Secretary.” Trump’s “confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country,” she wrote. “The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day.” Zacharia currently serves as a senior communications advisor to Trump Media and Technology Group, which operates the president’s Truth Social platform. Trump described her work at his company as “outstanding.” A frequent commentator on conservative television networks including Fox News and Newsmax, Zacharia previously served a brief stint as a spokeswoman for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees US immigration enforcement. – High profile role – She joined the department under then-secretary Kristi Noem earlier this year but left after around two months, according to her LinkedIn profile. Zacharia, who lives in California, has also worked with Fix California, a conservative advocacy group founded by Richard Grenell, a longtime Trump ally and one of his special presidential envoys. According to CNBC, she serves as general counsel for the organization, which seeks to advance conservative political causes in the Democratic-leaning state. A graduate of Pepperdine University’s law school, Zacharia began her career in Republican politics, working as an intern for the Republican National Committee in 2006, CNN reported. Trump sought advice from several allies and advisors, including Leavitt, before deciding to offer Zacharia the position, according to CNN. Her appointment fills one of the White House’s most visible positions, with the press secretary responsible for briefing journalists, fielding questions about administration policies and serving as a chief public defender of the president. Leavitt, who took up the position when Trump returned to power in January 2025, became the youngest White House press secretary in US history at 27. A staunch Trump loyalist who previously served as press secretary for his 2024 presidential campaign, she left the administration in late August following the birth of her second child. Fox News announced this week that Leavitt would join the conservative network as an on-air contributor beginning in November. Trump praised his outgoing spokeswoman, saying she had done a “fantastic job” in the role. AFP The post Trump appoints ‘devoted fan’ Katie Zacharia as press secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Owerri Airport to close for 25 days for runway rehabilitation ahead of Christmas – FG
items.description: Federal Government, in collaboration with the Imo State Government, will temporarily close the Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport in Owerri for approximately 25 days starting October 20, 2026, to carry out essential runway repairs and extension works. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, announced the closure in a press statement, emphasizing that the intervention is critical to ensure aviation safety, increase capacity, and improve operational efficiency ahead of the traditional surge in Christmas travel to the South-East. The rehabilitation project will address deteriorated sections of the runway pavement, treat extensive surface cracks, and fill potholes. Alongside resurfacing, the planned runway extension aims to upgrade the airport’s capacity to accommodate larger, wide-body aircraft, subject to regulatory requirements. The decision follows an agreement between the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Imo State Governor Senator Hope Uzodinma, and other regional stakeholders. Keyamo praised the partnership between the federal and state governments, noting that a modernized airport will serve as a critical gateway for businesses and support the economic development of the region. Addressing the inevitable disruptions, the Ministry acknowledged the inconvenience the closure will cause to airport users but stressed that aviation safety cannot be compromised. The temporary shutdown is necessary to allow contractors unhindered access to effectively execute the upgrades. Passengers scheduled to travel through Owerri during the 25-day closure period are advised to contact their respective airlines immediately to arrange for flight cancellations, rescheduling, or alternative travel plans. The government has pledged to continue engaging with airlines and stakeholders to minimize disruptions, with confirmed reopening dates to be communicated through official channels. The post Owerri Airport to close for 25 days for runway rehabilitation ahead of Christmas – FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Man City guilty verdict reignites Liverpool rivalry
items.description: Manchester City will face the full fury of Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League leaders confront old rivals Liverpool in their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial rules. City can expect a hostile reception from Liverpool fans after an independent commission found they arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) between 2009 and 2018. The financial breaches occurred during a period in which City won three Premier League titles and numerous other trophies, with Liverpool struggling to break the Etihad Stadium outfit’s silverware monopoly. City have appealed against the devastating verdict and manager Enzo Maresca was bullish on Friday that they will overturn the original ruling. But the Premier League season is now stuck in stasis awaiting a ruling on the appeal and any potential sanction. “I think the worst thing probably is the uncertainty, that no one knows what’s going to happen,” Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said on Friday. A severe points penalty leading to relegation or even expulsion from the English top flight are on the table, while there is also speculation City could be stripped of titles. “I think they have to be stripped of the titles. Otherwise you send the wrong message to anyone in the future,” John Gibbons of Liverpool podcast The Anfield Wrap told AFP. “There can’t be any trust now, certainly not if there’s not an admission of guilt. For me, I don’t see how Manchester City continue in the league.” Over the past 12 years, Liverpool have finished second to City on three occasions. Only one of those in 2013/14 came during the period under scrutiny. But City’s rivals believe the wrongdoing in that period built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who stepped down at the end of last season. – ‘Not playing by same rules’ – Twice Jurgen Klopp’s Reds missed out on the title despite amassing over 90 points. Those title battles turned meetings between City and Liverpool into English football’s marquee event and the eyes of the world will be on Anfield again come Sunday. “It just shows how remarkable that team that Jurgen Klopp built was and what they were up against,” added Gibbons. “They were obviously going against another side who it has been shown weren’t playing by the same rules as everyone else.” Even in happier times, City have rarely enjoyed their trips to Anfield. Last season’s 2-1 victory was City’s first win there in front of a crowd since 2003, with their other win coming amid Covid-19 restrictions in 2021. City return to Anfield sitting top of the Premier League after a flawless start to Maresca’s reign, featuring seven successive wins in all competitions. Just months after the charges against the club were first announced in February 2023, City went on to win the treble, clinching the club’s first Champions League crown, as well as the Premier League and FA Cup. The question is whether Maresca’s men can tap into that siege mentality once more, rather than wilting under the intense scrutiny. Liverpool supporters have often created a febrile atmosphere for City’s visits since they emerged as title contenders following the takeover by their Abu Dhabi-based owners in 2008. This weekend’s showdown is likely to set a new standard for vitriol directed at City’s players and fans. “It’s going to be massively hostile,” said Dom Farrell, author of the book “Glory Days for the Waifs and Strays” that chronicled City’s rise from the third tier to European champions. “If they were to win against Liverpool and then beat an off-form Paris Saint-Germain you really get a siege mentality going. “But there’s also a decent chance they get turned over and then it just starts to feel you’re in this sort of dead zone waiting for the verdict.” AFP The post Man City guilty verdict reignites Liverpool rivalry appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Three months to polls, campaigns, rallies yet to begin
items.description: By Clifford Ndujihe THREE months to the 2027 general elections, political parties and their candidates are yet to fully hit the streets for campaigns, despite the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, opening the campaign window nearly two months ago. According to the commission’s timetable, the Presidential and National Assembly polls will be held on January 16, 2027 while those of the governorship and state houses of assembly will take place, three weeks later, on February 6, 2027. INEC cleared the way for Presidential and National Assembly elections campaigns last August 19 and that of the governorship and state assemblies, September 9. Since then, no serious campaigns have commenced. A couple of the leading parties have raised their Presidential Campaign Councils, PCCs, most are yet to do so. As it is, exactly 97 days to the Presidential and NASS polls, and 118 days to the governorship and state assembly balloting, no party or candidate has unveiled his/her or its campaign plan and itinerary. Unlike previous election cycles, when streets would, at this stage, be awash with posters and billboards and candidates would be criss-crossing their constituencies, in an unmistakable poster war, the current political atmosphere is relatively subdued. Now, the scenario is different as Saturday Vanguard’s checks across the country show. Only a handful of leading parties have constituted campaign councils, while many candidates are concentrating on consultations, grassroots mobilisation, party structures and legal battles. But where campaigns have begun, another battle is emerging — the struggle for billboards and other public advertising spaces, with allegations of removal, destruction, intimidation and partisan use of regulatory powers. APC crisis stalls poster war in Ondo Political activities remain low in Ondo State, with only a few APC candidates displaying posters at strategic locations. Unlike previous election seasons, there is no poster war, as candidates of opposition parties are largely absent from the streets. Investigations showed that only a handful of opposition candidates have pasted posters, while many are yet to print theirs. The development has been linked largely to the crisis within the APC, where several aspirants who lost the party’s primaries have gone to court to challenge the outcome. Even among incumbent National Assembly members who secured return tickets, only a few have printed and displayed campaign posters. The uncertainty surrounding candidacies has therefore slowed political activities. The APC National Working Committee had dropped some aspirants after the primaries, triggering fresh crisis and litigation, which have combined to prevent the usual billboard and poster war. Meanwhile, billboards bearing the image of APC presidential candidate, Senator Bola Tinubu, are prominent across major towns and roads, while only a few posters of ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Abubakar Atiku, are visible. Another factor is that there will be no governorship election in Ondo in 2027. The state will vote in the presidential, National Assembly and State Assembly elections. Tinubu dominates Ekiti The situation is similar in Ekiti, where the campaign landscape remains markedly different from the intense poster and billboard competition normally associated with elections. Tinubu’s posters and billboards are prominent across several locations, while the presence of opposition parties, particularly ADC and NDC, remains subdued. A major political development is the decision of Dr Wole Oluyede, who contested the June 20, 2026 governorship election on the PDP platform, to support Tinubu’s re-election. Oluyede has established the Oluyede Progressive Alliance for Renewed Hope Agenda, OPARHA, to mobilise support for Tinubu across the state’s 16 local government areas and 177 wards. At a mobilisation rally in Ado-Ekiti, Oluyede and Governor Biodun Oyebanji jointly canvassed support for Tinubu and pledged to work for at least 90 per cent of the President’s votes in Ekiti. For now, the physical campaign landscape is heavily tilted towards Tinubu and the APC. Osun: No defacing of posters Osun presents a different picture. Campaign posters and banners are being displayed competitively without the widespread defacing that characterised the August governorship election. Different parties have mounted campaign materials at public places without reports of widespread destruction. The development contrasts sharply with the recent governorship election, which witnessed extensive destruction of posters and billboards belonging to major political parties. Billboard war, opposition cries foul in Lagos In Lagos, political activities are taking place amid heightened tension, early mobilisation and strict regulation of public advertising space. The governorship contest involving the APC, ADC and PDP is attracting more attention than the Senate, House of Representatives and State Assembly contests, which remain relatively subdued. APC governorship candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and his running mate, Princess Damilola Sonayon-James, have established a strong presence, alongside President Tinubu. Billboards bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and Hamzat are prominent in Ikeja, Alausa, the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, Obalende and around the Third Mainland Bridge. The posters, which began appearing in August, are also visible around Agege, Alimosho and other areas. By contrast, billboards of ADC presidential candidate and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, as well as NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, are yet to achieve comparable visibility. The opposition has alleged harassment and removal of its campaign materials. NDC supporters accused the Lagos State Signage and Advertisement Agency, LASAA, of removing more than 50 banners belonging to Peter Obi and House of Representatives candidate, Dr Adefolaseye Adebomi, in Surulere while leaving APC materials intact. NDC chieftain, Aisha Yesufu, condemned the alleged action, describing it as the behaviour of a party that is “scared, desperate, and crumbling rather than one in control.” She also criticised the high cost of billboard advertising, alleging that fees running into hundreds of millions of naira were being imposed in some areas. The Lagos State Government had yet to respond to the allegation at the time of filing this report. Campaign materials under attack in Ogun Political activities are gathering momentum in Ogun, with the PDP formally commencing its governorship campaign and the ruling APC intensifying mobilisation across the three senatorial districts. But posters, banners and billboards mounted in public spaces are increasingly being vandalised. Some campaign materials have been torn down, defaced or damaged, with different parties and candidates reportedly affected. The development has raised concerns as the parties intensify grassroots engagement and public messaging ahead of the elections. The growing appearance of campaign materials on major roads and in communities has already transformed parts of the state into political battlegrounds, even though the full campaign season is yet to peak. Battle for visibility moves to billboards in Oyo In Oyo State, the struggle for political visibility is gradually moving to the streets, particularly billboards and posters. Across Ibadan and other areas, campaign materials of prominent contenders have begun appearing at strategic locations, although the state is yet to witness a full-scale poster war. Controversy erupted in July when the ADC alleged that a billboard belonging to its governorship candidate, Olooye Taofeek Adegboyega Adegoke, at Idi-Ape Junction, Ibadan, was removed and replaced with materials bearing the images of Governor Seyi Makinde and APM governorship candidate, Bimbo Adekanmbi. Adegoke said: “My money is still running on that billboard till 20th August 2026.” The APM denied responsibility, attributing billboard disputes to advertising agencies and regulatory authorities. The APC later raised similar allegations, claiming that some of its billboards for governorship candidate, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, were being removed or destroyed. APM again denied involvement, saying: “We do not destroy opponents’ materials, we do not sponsor thuggery, and we do not engage in violence.” For now, Oyo’s contest is still at the early stage of the battle for public attention, with candidates also relying on radio, television, social media, rallies and consultations. Candidates stake claims in Delta Campaign activities in Delta are yet to fully take off, but the political atmosphere is warming up as aspirants intensify consultations with party leaders, traditional rulers, community leaders and supporters. Posters and billboards belonging to candidates are becoming increasingly visible in Asaba and other major towns, but the development has not translated into a full-blown poster war. Political actors are adopting a cautious approach, seeking to establish visibility while strengthening party structures and grassroots networks. For many candidates, consultations and mobilisation are currently more important than committing huge resources to full-scale advertising. The gradual appearance of posters and billboards, however, indicates that the 2027 contest is entering the public consciousness. Complaints of billboard destruction rein in Edo Political activities are picking up across Edo’s three senatorial districts, with junctions and public spaces increasingly competing for campaign posters and banners. The APC has inaugurated its campaign council, while Governor Monday Okpebholo, his deputy, Dennis Idahosa, and party leaders have commenced mobilisation visits to the state’s 18 local government areas. The NDC is also campaigning but has complained about attacks on its posters. The party’s candidate for Akoko-Edo II State Constituency, Paul Alaba Lawani, said the NDC was prepared to defeat the incumbent through its grassroots strength. Other active campaign groups include the Chief Thomas Attah Movement, backing Dr Thomas Attah’s House of Representatives ambition in Akoko-Edo Federal Constituency, and the Abbaas Naasamu campaign team of the ADC. However, the campaign has already recorded an allegation of political violence. Suspected political thugs allegedly attacked the campaign office of NDC candidate for Oredo Federal Constituency, Hon Frank Uyi Omosigho, in Benin City. Several campaign materials at the Stadium Road office were pulled down and damaged. Omosigho said youths alerted him to the attack and urged young people not to allow politicians to use them to perpetrate violence. “My appeal to youths is not to allow politicians to use them to perpetrate violence or other illegal acts. Anyone caught violating the law would face the consequences,” he said. He added: “The campaign materials were meant to introduce candidates and political parties to the electorate. The voters had the right to make their choices independently.”The incident was reported to the police, while the Commissioner of Police and Department of State Services, DSS, were also informed. Another NDC candidate, St Moses Eromosele, has similarly complained that his billboards were being pulled down and accused the APC. With the elections drawing closer, the subdued campaign atmosphere across the eight states may soon give way to the familiar frenzy of rallies, posters, billboards and political mobilisation. For now, however, the battle is being fought largely behind the scenes — in party meetings, courtrooms, consultations and the increasingly contested public spaces where candidates seek to make their first impressions on voters. Dayo Johnson, Olasunkanmi Akoni, Egufe Yafugborhi, Rotimi Ojomoyela, Ozioruva Aliu, Shina Abubakar, James Ogunnnaike & Adeola Badru contributed to this report Vanguard News The post 2027: Three months to polls, campaigns, rallies yet to begin appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gestion de l’état civil : Une délégation du ministère en charge de l’Administration territoriale échange avec les acteurs locaux de la commune Avé 1
items.description: Kévé, 9 oct. (ATOP) – Une délégation du ministère de l’Administration territoriale, de la Gouvernance locale et des Affaires coutumières, conduite par le chef de division de la présentation territoriale de l’État, Blivi Adoté Mawulolo a échangé avec les acteurs locaux de la commune Avé 1 sur la gestion de l’état civil, le jeudi 8 octobre dans la localité. La rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du processus de relecture de la loi du 11 juin 2009 relative à l’organisation de l’état civil au Togo. Elle vise à renforcer la compréhension des dispositions en vigueur, à recueillir les difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain et à collecter les contributions des acteurs en vue de l’adaptation du cadre juridique aux réalités actuelles. Les discussions ont porté sur les procédures d’établissement et de gestion des actes de naissance, de mariage et de décès, ainsi que sur les questions relatives à la rectification des actes, aux mentions et à la transmission des informations entre les services compétents. Les participants ont notamment relevé les difficultés liées à la détermination du lieu de déclaration d’une naissance lorsque celui-ci ne correspond pas au lieu de naissance ou au lieu de résidence des parents. L’importance de l’acte de naissance dans l’identification juridique de la personne et l’accès à plusieurs droits et services a également été soulignée. L’accent a été mis sur l’acte de mariage, qui établit juridiquement le lien matrimonial, et l’acte de décès, nécessaire à la mise à jour de la situation juridique du défunt. Des éclaircissements ont été apportés aux préoccupations soulevées par les acteurs de terrain. La digitalisation de l’état civil a, par ailleurs, été évoquée comme un levier de modernisation du système. Elle doit permettre d’améliorer l’enregistrement et la conservation des actes, de sécuriser les données et de faciliter leur transmission entre les services compétents. Les préoccupations et propositions recueillies au cours de la rencontre vont contribuer à parfaire le processus de relecture de la législation. Le but est de disposer d’un cadre juridique mieux adapté aux réalités actuelles et aux exigences liées à la décentralisation, à la digitalisation et à la sécurisation de l’identité. La rencontre a réuni le personnel de la mairie, des autorités administratives et locales, des représentants d’institutions publiques et privées, des organisations non gouvernementales (ONG), ainsi que d’autres acteurs intervenant dans la gestion et l’utilisation des actes d’état civil.
